text.text: A project goes wrong at the start far more often than at the end. Kickoff is where scope, people and risks get written down.
With the client
Agree the goal in one sentence
List the three must-have features
Name the client's single decision maker
Set the meeting rhythm and the change request process
Inside the agency
Create the project row and add milestones
Book design, build and QA time
Set up repositories, tracker and a test device list
Agree what 'done' means for each milestone
Shipping is a ritual: the same steps every time, so no one has to remember them under pressure.
A week before
Open the project's Release check and clear every critical bug
Freeze features; only fixes from now on
Run the regression pass on real devices
Prepare release notes and store text
Release day
Upload the build and submit for review
Watch crash reports for the first 24 hours
Tell the client the moment the store approves
Press Mark launched
Changes are normal. Unwritten changes are what turn a good project into an argument.
Process
Write the request as a short story: who wants what and why.
Estimate the effort in hours and the effect on the date.
Send the client the estimate and wait for a written yes.
Add the work as a milestone so progress stays honest.
Say yes with a price
A good answer is rarely no. It is yes, here is what it costs and what moves.
